docket.VOTE: On 18 November 2024 at the Security Council's 9786th meeting, draft S/2024/826, submitted by Sierra Leone and the United Kingdom, received 14 votes in favour, one against and no abstentions. China voted in favour. The Russian Federation cast the sole negative vote. The Council did not adopt the draft because a permanent member voted against.
docket.TEXT: The proposed text concerned ending hostilities in Sudan, protecting civilians and facilitating humanitarian access. The vote did not adopt these measures in S/2024/826.

Russian Federation.RU-A: Dmitry Polyanskiy criticized the proposed text as creating a route for outside interference in Sudan. He opposed using external accountability mechanisms and argued that administration of justice should remain with the Government of Sudan.
Russian Federation.RU-B: Polyanskiy argued that humanitarian measures needed agreement with Sudan's central authorities. He called for time and political space for Personal Envoy Ramtane Lamamra to engage relevant actors.

China.CN-A: Fu Cong supported an immediate ceasefire and de-escalation to protect civilians and explained that this was why China voted in favour. He also said some constructive proposals and concerns had not been fully reflected.
China.CN-B: Fu emphasized Sudanese sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, and said Council action should rest on consultation with Sudan's Government and other relevant parties. He supported the Personal Envoy's coordination with the African Union and regional organizations.

disposition: Names draft S/2024/826 and both sponsors and records non-adoption.
Gives 14–1–0, identifies Russia's sole no and attributes non-adoption to its permanent-member negative vote.
operative_action: Describes the proposed cessation of hostilities and civilian protection without asserting that either was adopted.
Preserves the proposed facilitation of humanitarian access.
positions_and_reasons: Attributes Russia's concern about external interference or exclusive national accountability authority to its representative.
Preserves China's affirmative vote, ceasefire and civilian-protection rationale and stated reservations about the text.
overlap_and_open_issues: Identifies limited common ground in involving Sudanese authorities or supporting the Personal Envoy, with each role's different caveats intact.
Preserves the different recorded positions on the draft and distinguishes common diplomatic aims from assent to the text.
authority_and_scope: Separates the unadopted text from any existing Council mandate.
Presents any suggested next action as analysis and does not attribute a new joint commitment to either delegation.
